title: ABAP ALV: SALV framework para listas modernas
tags: abap, alv, salv, list, report, gui
excerpt: SALV — framework OO moderno para mostrar tablas en SAP GUI.
body:
## ALV framework
SAP List Viewer — muestra tablas con features estándar:
- Sort, filter, group
- Export a Excel/PDF
- Sum, subtotals
- Print
- Layout variants

## SALV (moderno, OO)
Reemplaza REUSE_ALV_* (function modules legacy).

### Ejemplo mínimo
```abap
REPORT z_alv_demo.

DATA: lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight WITH DEFAULT KEY.

SELECT * FROM sflight INTO TABLE @lt_data UP TO 100 ROWS.

TRY.
    cl_salv_table=>factory(
        IMPORTING r_salv_table = DATA(lo_alv)
        CHANGING t_table = lt_data ).

    lo_alv->display( ).

CATCH cx_salv_msg INTO DATA(lx).
    MESSAGE lx TYPE 'E'.
ENDTRY.
```

Con esas ~10 líneas mostrás una lista con toolbar completa.

## Configuraciones comunes

### Toolbar functions
```abap
DATA(lo_functions) = lo_alv->get_functions( ).
lo_functions->set_all( abap_true ).   " activate all standard functions
```

### Column settings
```abap
DATA(lo_columns) = lo_alv->get_columns( ).
lo_columns->set_optimize( abap_true ).   " auto-width

DATA(lo_col_carrid) = lo_columns->get_column( 'CARRID' ).
lo_col_carrid->set_short_text( 'Aerol.' ).
lo_col_carrid->set_medium_text( 'Aerolínea' ).
lo_col_carrid->set_long_text( 'Código de aerolínea' ).
lo_col_carrid->set_output_length( 10 ).
```

### Hide column
```abap
lo_col_price->set_visible( abap_false ).
```

### Colored rows
```abap
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_row,
           carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
           price TYPE s_price,
           color TYPE lvc_t_scol,   " color info
       END OF ty_row.

DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_row.

" ...poblar lt_data...
LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<row>).
    IF <row>-price > 500.
        APPEND VALUE #( color = 6 ) TO <row>-color.   " rojo
    ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.

" ...factory + display
DATA(lo_columns) = lo_alv->get_columns( ).
lo_columns->set_color_column( 'COLOR' ).
```

### Layouts
```abap
DATA(lo_layout) = lo_alv->get_layout( ).
lo_layout->set_key( VALUE salv_s_layout_key( report = sy-repid ) ).
lo_layout->set_save_restriction( if_salv_c_layout=>restrict_none ).
```

Usuarios guardan layouts personales.

### Sort default
```abap
DATA(lo_sorts) = lo_alv->get_sorts( ).
lo_sorts->add_sort( columnname = 'PRICE' sequence = if_salv_c_sort=>sort_down ).
```

### Aggregations (SUM)
```abap
DATA(lo_aggregations) = lo_alv->get_aggregations( ).
lo_aggregations->add_aggregation( columnname = 'PRICE' aggregation = if_salv_c_aggregation=>total ).
```

## Events (interactive)
### Click en row
```abap
CLASS lcl_handler DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS on_double_click FOR EVENT double_click OF cl_salv_events_table
            IMPORTING row column.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_handler IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD on_double_click.
        " abre transacción con el key del row
        DATA(ls_row) = <lt_data>[ row ].
        SET PARAMETER ID 'CARRID' FIELD ls_row-carrid.
        CALL TRANSACTION 'BC_ATRA'.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

" en el programa principal
DATA(lo_events) = lo_alv->get_event( ).
DATA(lo_handler) = NEW lcl_handler( ).
SET HANDLER lo_handler->on_double_click FOR lo_events.
```

### Toolbar button custom
```abap
DATA(lo_functions) = lo_alv->get_functions( ).
lo_functions->add_function(
    name = 'EXPORT_CUSTOM'
    icon = space
    text = 'Exportar a XLS custom'
    tooltip = 'Exporta con formato específico'
    position = if_salv_c_function_position=>right_of_salv_functions
).

" handler
METHOD on_user_command FOR EVENT added_function OF cl_salv_events_table
    IMPORTING e_salv_function.
    CASE e_salv_function.
        WHEN 'EXPORT_CUSTOM'.
            " custom export logic
    ENDCASE.
ENDMETHOD.
```

## SALV Tree (jerárquico)
Para datos jerárquicos:
```abap
cl_salv_tree=>factory(
    IMPORTING r_salv_tree = DATA(lo_tree)
    CHANGING t_table = lt_data ).
```

## SALV Hierseq (jerárquico secuencial)
Master-detail:
```abap
cl_salv_hierseq_table=>factory(
    IMPORTING r_hierseq = DATA(lo_hierseq)
    CHANGING t_table1 = lt_headers   " master
             t_table2 = lt_items    " detail
).
```

## Export
### Excel
Botón standard en toolbar → Export → Local file → Spreadsheet.

### Programmatic export
```abap
DATA(lo_export) = lo_alv->to_xml( ).   " XML representation
" O usar CL_SALV_EXPORT_TO_XLS
```

## SALV vs REUSE_ALV_GRID_DISPLAY (legacy)
### REUSE_ALV_*
- Function-based
- Muchos parameters
- Menos flexible
- Still supported pero old

### SALV
- OO clean
- Menos código
- Mejor performance
- Recomendado para new development

## Common issues

### 'Columns misaligned'
- Structure de lt_data no matchea display
- Verificar TYPE del ITAB

### 'Fields aren't showing'
- Estructura tiene fields que ALV desconoce → set_visible( false )
- O incluir en fieldcatalog manualmente

### 'Slow con muchos rows'
- Grid mode consume memoria
- Considerar paging o filter primero

### 'Layout no persiste'
- Missing `set_key` 
- User sin auth para variants públicas

## Autorización
- `S_ALV_LAYO` — layout maintenance

## Best practices
- **SALV over REUSE_ALV_*** siempre para new dev
- **set_optimize + set_short_text/long_text** — mejor UX
- **Layout variants** habilitados
- **Events handled carefully** — memory leaks si no cleanup
- **Aggregations pre-configuradas** en reports typical
- **Cascade layout con SM30** para defaults corporativos

title: ABAP: dialog programming (dynpros — screens)
tags: abap, dynpro, screen, pbo, pai, dialog
excerpt: Programación de screens (dynpros) — GUI clásico ABAP.
body:
## Dynpro
**Dynamic Program** — screen ABAP. Módulos PBO (Process Before Output) + PAI (Process After Input).

Base de transactional apps clásicas (SU01, MM03, FB50, etc.). Legacy pero muy usado.

## Componentes
### Screen
- Diseño gráfico (Screen Painter, SE51)
- Elementos: input fields, buttons, checkboxes, radio buttons, tables (table control)

### Flow logic
```
PROCESS BEFORE OUTPUT.
    MODULE status_0100.
    MODULE populate_data.

PROCESS AFTER INPUT.
    MODULE user_command_0100.
    MODULE validate_input.
```

### Modules (en programa principal)
```abap
MODULE status_0100 OUTPUT.
    SET PF-STATUS 'STATUS_0100'.
    SET TITLEBAR 'TITLE_0100'.
ENDMODULE.

MODULE user_command_0100 INPUT.
    CASE sy-ucomm.
        WHEN 'SAVE'.
            PERFORM save_data.
        WHEN 'BACK' OR 'CANCEL' OR 'EXIT'.
            LEAVE PROGRAM.
    ENDCASE.
ENDMODULE.
```

## Screen elements
### Input field
Define en screen painter:
- Name: `GS_HEADER-PRODUCT_ID`
- Type: automatic desde ABAP dictionary
- Length, dropdown, F4 help

Variable en ABAP:
```abap
DATA: BEGIN OF gs_header,
          product_id TYPE mara-matnr,
          name       TYPE string,
          price      TYPE p LENGTH 10 DECIMALS 2,
      END OF gs_header.
```

### Button
En screen painter agregás button con:
- Function code: `SAVE`, `CANCEL`, etc.

En PAI, `sy-ucomm` tiene el function code presionado.

### Checkbox / radio button
```abap
DATA gv_active TYPE c LENGTH 1.
" Screen: field name = GV_ACTIVE, type = checkbox
```

### Table control
Mostrar tabla en screen (parecido a ALV pero más flexible):
```abap
CONTROLS tc_items TYPE TABLEVIEW USING SCREEN 100.
DATA gt_items TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item.
```

En el screen painter dibujás la tabla + defines columns.

En flow logic:
```
PROCESS BEFORE OUTPUT.
    LOOP AT gt_items INTO gs_item WITH CONTROL tc_items.
        MODULE display_item.
    ENDLOOP.

PROCESS AFTER INPUT.
    LOOP AT gt_items.
        MODULE process_item.
    ENDLOOP.
```

## PF-STATUS
Menu bar + toolbar + function keys de la screen:
1. Doble clic en 'STATUS_0100' en tu module o crear con SE41
2. Screen painter → **Menu Bar**, **Standard Toolbar**, **Application Toolbar**
3. Assign function codes a cada opción

### Function codes clave
- **BACK** (F3), **CANCEL** (F12), **EXIT** (Shift+F3)
- **SAVE** (Ctrl+S)
- Custom: `NEW`, `DELETE`, `SEARCH`, etc.

## Titlebar
1. Doble clic en 'TITLE_0100' en el module
2. Texto que aparece en top de la ventana
3. Placeholders: `Sales Order &1` donde &1 se rellena en runtime

## Modificar comportamiento en runtime

### Ocultar fields dinámicamente
```abap
LOOP AT SCREEN.
    IF screen-name = 'GS_HEADER-PRICE' AND gv_role <> 'ADMIN'.
        screen-active = 0.  " hide field
    ENDIF.
    IF screen-group1 = 'ADM' AND gv_role <> 'ADMIN'.
        screen-invisible = 1.
    ENDIF.
    MODIFY SCREEN.
ENDLOOP.
```

### Read-only en runtime
```abap
screen-input = 0.
MODIFY SCREEN.
```

## Navegación entre screens
### Call screen
```abap
CALL SCREEN 200.   " abre en modo modal
```

### Set screen + leave screen
```abap
SET SCREEN 200.
LEAVE SCREEN.
```

### Leave to screen
```abap
LEAVE TO SCREEN 100.   " al screen 100 sin volver
```

## F4 help programático
```abap
MODULE f4_product_id INPUT.
    CALL FUNCTION 'F4IF_INT_TABLE_VALUE_REQUEST'
        EXPORTING retfield = 'MATNR'
                 window_title = 'Seleccione Material'
                 value_org = 'S'
        TABLES value_tab = gt_help_values
               return_tab = lt_return.

    READ TABLE lt_return INTO DATA(ls_return) INDEX 1.
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
        gs_header-product_id = ls_return-fieldval.
    ENDIF.
ENDMODULE.
```

En el screen field property: 'Value help' → link al module.

## Message handling
```abap
MESSAGE 'Precio inválido' TYPE 'E'.   " error stops flow
MESSAGE 'Guardado OK' TYPE 'S'.       " success al footer
MESSAGE 'Advertencia' TYPE 'W'.       " warning
MESSAGE 'Info' TYPE 'I'.              " info dialog
MESSAGE 'Fatal' TYPE 'A'.             " abort
```

### Con message class
```abap
MESSAGE i001(zmymsg) WITH gs_header-product_id.
```

ID `ZMYMSG` message 001 con placeholder.

## Screen field validation
```abap
MODULE validate_product INPUT.
    SELECT SINGLE matnr FROM mara INTO @gs_header-product_id
        WHERE matnr = @gs_header-product_id.
    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        MESSAGE 'Material no existe' TYPE 'E'.
    ENDIF.
ENDMODULE.
```

En flow logic:
```
CHAIN.
    FIELD gs_header-product_id.
    MODULE validate_product ON CHAIN-INPUT.
ENDCHAIN.
```

## Common issues

### 'Screen no muestra field'
- Field no está en screen (verificar SE51)
- Group1/Group2 grupo hidden en runtime
- `screen-active = 0` en LOOP AT SCREEN

### 'Function code doesn't fire'
- PF-STATUS no configurado
- Function code wrong en PF-STATUS

### 'Message no aparece'
- Type not appropriate
- Wrong client (mandante)

### 'Table control blank'
- gt_items not populated
- LOOP AT en flow logic missing

## Modern alternatives

### Web Dynpro
OO screens web-based. Deprecating (SAP move to Fiori).

### Fiori (Web)
HTML5 + OData. Moderna, responsive.

### Screen painter still relevant
SAP GUI transactions siguen usando dynpros. Miles de programas legacy.

## Best practices
- **Modularity** — separate flow logic en modules pequeños
- **PBO for output, PAI for input** — no mezclar responsibility
- **Validate en PAI** — antes de acceptar transiciones
- **Standard function codes** — BACK/CANCEL/EXIT consistentes
- **F4 help útil** — mejor UX
- **Message class ZMYMSG** — traducible + reusable

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` — crear/editar
- `S_TCODE` — ejecutar transacciones

## Alternativas para new dev
Fiori Elements con RAP > dynpros. Legacy code se mantiene por ahora.

title: ABAP selection screens: PARAMETERS + SELECT-OPTIONS
tags: abap, selection screen, parameters, select-options, report
excerpt: Diseño de pantalla de selección en reports ABAP.
body:
## Selection screen
Pantalla de entrada al inicio de un report. Estándar en programas tipo `REPORT`.

## PARAMETERS
Field único de entrada:

```abap
PARAMETERS: p_matnr TYPE mara-matnr,
            p_werks TYPE marc-werks OBLIGATORY,
            p_date  TYPE sy-datum DEFAULT sy-datum,
            p_check AS CHECKBOX,
            p_radio RADIOBUTTON GROUP grp1 DEFAULT 'X',
            p_radio2 RADIOBUTTON GROUP grp1.
```

Options:
- `OBLIGATORY` — user debe completar
- `DEFAULT` — valor pre-llenado
- `LOWER CASE` — no convertir a mayúsculas
- `AS CHECKBOX` — checkbox
- `RADIOBUTTON GROUP` — botón radio (una opción por grupo)

## SELECT-OPTIONS
Range (from/to + include/exclude), múltiples valores:

```abap
SELECT-OPTIONS: s_matnr FOR mara-matnr,
                s_werks FOR marc-werks OBLIGATORY,
                s_date  FOR sy-datum DEFAULT sy-datum TO sy-datum.
```

Al ejecutar user puede:
- **Single value**: 100000
- **Range**: 100000 to 200000
- **Multiple singles**: 100000, 100500, 100800
- **Complex**: 100000 to 200000 excluyendo 100500

Se usa en WHERE:
```abap
SELECT * FROM mara INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_mara)
    WHERE matnr IN @s_matnr
      AND werks IN @s_werks.
```

## Screen blocks (agrupación visual)
```abap
SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b1 WITH FRAME TITLE text-b01.
PARAMETERS: p_matnr TYPE mara-matnr,
            p_werks TYPE marc-werks.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b1.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b2 WITH FRAME TITLE text-b02.
SELECT-OPTIONS: s_date FOR sy-datum.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b2.
```

text-b01, text-b02: text symbols del programa (SE38 → menu Goto → Text elements).

## Multiple screens (tabs)
```abap
SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF TABBED BLOCK tb FOR 10 LINES.
SELECTION-SCREEN TAB (20) tab1 USER-COMMAND ucm1 DEFAULT SCREEN 100.
SELECTION-SCREEN TAB (20) tab2 USER-COMMAND ucm2 DEFAULT SCREEN 200.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK tb.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF SCREEN 100 AS SUBSCREEN.
PARAMETERS p_x TYPE i.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF SCREEN 100.
```

Pestañas en pantalla de selección.

## Layout controls

### Comentarios + text elements
```abap
SELECTION-SCREEN COMMENT /1(30) text-c01.   " línea completa
SELECTION-SCREEN COMMENT 5(20) text-c02.    " en línea actual, offset 5
```

### Ubicación explícita
```abap
SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF LINE.
SELECTION-SCREEN COMMENT 1(20) text-l01.
PARAMETERS: p_val TYPE i.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF LINE.
```

### Skip lines
```abap
SELECTION-SCREEN SKIP.
SELECTION-SCREEN SKIP 2.
```

## Ejecución con variant
Usuario puede save variants (combinaciones de valores):

### Save variant
1. Selection screen → completar valores
2. Menú **Goto → Variants → Save**
3. Nombre + description

### Load variant
1. Menú **Get variant** o F17
2. Seleccionar

### Programmatic
```abap
SUBMIT z_report USING SELECTION-SET 'MI_VARIANT'
    AND RETURN.
```

## Events específicos

### AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT
Antes de mostrar screen — ajustes visuales:
```abap
AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT.
    LOOP AT SCREEN.
        IF screen-group1 = 'ADM' AND sy-uname <> 'ADMIN_USER'.
            screen-active = 0.
            MODIFY SCREEN.
        ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
```

### AT SELECTION-SCREEN
Antes de ejecutar (validación):
```abap
AT SELECTION-SCREEN.
    IF p_werks IS INITIAL.
        MESSAGE 'Plant es obligatorio' TYPE 'E'.
    ENDIF.
```

### AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON <field>
Validación específica de un field:
```abap
AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON p_matnr.
    SELECT SINGLE @abap_true FROM mara INTO @DATA(lv_exists)
        WHERE matnr = @p_matnr.
    IF lv_exists = abap_false.
        MESSAGE 'Material no existe' TYPE 'E'.
    ENDIF.
```

### AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON VALUE-REQUEST FOR <field>
F4 help custom:
```abap
AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON VALUE-REQUEST FOR p_matnr.
    CALL FUNCTION 'F4IF_INT_TABLE_VALUE_REQUEST'
        EXPORTING retfield = 'MATNR'
        TABLES value_tab = gt_helpvalues
               return_tab = lt_return.
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
        READ TABLE lt_return INTO DATA(ls_return) INDEX 1.
        p_matnr = ls_return-fieldval.
    ENDIF.
```

### AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON HELP-REQUEST FOR <field>
F1 help custom.

## Ejecución en background
Usuario puede clic **Execute in Background** (F9):
1. Job name
2. Printer settings
3. Start immediately o programado
4. Runs asynchronously

Requires selecting variant.

## Common issues

### 'PARAMETERS no aparece'
- Report tipo no `REPORT` (verificar cabecera)
- Compile error temprano

### 'Range no funciona correctamente'
- Sintaxis SELECT-OPTIONS incorrecta
- Field type mismatch

### 'Variants no cargan'
- Sin transporte
- User sin auth `S_DEVELOP` con VARI

### 'F4 help vacío'
- Table de helpvalues no populated
- Wrong retfield en el call

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` para crear/modificar reports
- Nada especial para ejecutar reports (except si el report tiene checks internos)

## Best practices
- **OBLIGATORY** en fields críticos
- **DEFAULT sensato** — sy-datum, sy-uname si aplicable
- **Validation en AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON** — antes de ejecutar
- **F4 help** — mejor UX
- **Variants public** para users frequentes
- **Text symbols** en lugar de hardcoded strings — traducibles
- **Documentation** con comentarios claros

title: ABAP internal tables: performance + patterns modernos
tags: abap, internal table, itab, performance, sorted, hashed
excerpt: Tipos de itabs, cuándo usar cada uno, patterns modernos.
body:
## Tipos de internal tables

### 1. Standard
```abap
DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_row.
```

- **Access**: por índice (`INDEX`)
- **Order**: mantiene orden de insert
- **Duplicates**: permitidos
- **Read time**: O(n) para búsqueda lineal, O(log n) con BINARY SEARCH después de SORT

Uso: mayoría de casos, iteración secuencial.

### 2. Sorted
```abap
DATA lt_data TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_row WITH UNIQUE KEY id.
DATA lt_data2 TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_row WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY id.
```

- **Access**: por key
- **Order**: automáticamente ordenado
- **Duplicates**: prohibidos (UNIQUE) o permitidos (NON-UNIQUE)
- **Read time**: O(log n) — binary search automático

Uso: acceso frecuente por key, poca inserción/borrado.

### 3. Hashed
```abap
DATA lt_data TYPE HASHED TABLE OF ty_row WITH UNIQUE KEY id.
```

- **Access**: solo por key (no índice)
- **Order**: no relevante
- **Duplicates**: prohibidos (siempre UNIQUE)
- **Read time**: O(1) — hash lookup

Uso: lookups repetidos por key, no requiere iteración ordenada.

### Comparativa
| | Standard | Sorted | Hashed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Insert | O(1) | O(log n) | O(1) |
| Delete by index | O(1) | O(log n) | N/A |
| Delete by key | O(n) | O(log n) | O(1) |
| Read by index | O(1) | O(1) | N/A |
| Read by key | O(n) o O(log n) | O(log n) | O(1) |
| Sort explícito | Necesario | No aplica | No aplica |
| Memory overhead | Bajo | Medio | Alto |

## Performance patterns

### 1. READ TABLE ... BINARY SEARCH
Solo funciona en tabla SORTED (por sort key) o STANDARD ordenada:

```abap
SORT lt_data BY id.

READ TABLE lt_data INTO DATA(ls_data)
    WITH KEY id = 12345
    BINARY SEARCH.
```

**Sin binary search** = O(n).
**Con** = O(log n).

Diferencia con 100k rows:
- Linear: ~50k comparaciones
- Binary: ~17 comparaciones

### 2. Secondary keys (ABAP 7.02+)
Standard/sorted table con secondary key hashed/sorted:

```abap
DATA lt_orders TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_order
    WITH DEFAULT KEY
    WITH UNIQUE SORTED KEY by_id COMPONENTS order_id
    WITH NON-UNIQUE HASHED KEY by_customer COMPONENTS customer_id.

READ TABLE lt_orders INTO DATA(ls_order)
    WITH TABLE KEY by_id
    COMPONENTS order_id = 12345.
```

Rápido lookup sin cambiar el tipo primary de la tabla.

### 3. Field symbols vs work areas
```abap
" Slow (copia)
LOOP AT lt_data INTO DATA(ls_data).
    ls_data-processed = 'X'.
    MODIFY lt_data FROM ls_data.
ENDLOOP.

" Fast (referencia)
LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_data>).
    <ls_data>-processed = 'X'.
ENDLOOP.
```

Field symbols evitan copia + MODIFY explícito.

### 4. LOOP AT ... WHERE
Filtro en el LOOP en vez de IF en cada iteración:

```abap
" Menos eficiente
LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING <row>.
    IF <row>-status = 'ACTIVE'.
        ...
    ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.

" Más eficiente (especialmente con SORTED table)
LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING <row> WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'.
    ...
ENDLOOP.
```

### 5. FOR ALL ENTRIES
Para SELECT con IN condition dinámico:

```abap
IF lt_orders IS NOT INITIAL.
    SELECT vbeln, kunnr FROM vbak
        FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
        WHERE vbeln = @lt_orders-order_id
        INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_headers).
ENDIF.
```

**Ojo**: SAP puede duplicar. Usar SORT + DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES después.

**Nunca** con tabla vacía — trae toda la tabla completa.

### 6. Table expressions (ABAP 7.40+)
Más legible + directo:

```abap
" Old style
READ TABLE lt_data INTO DATA(ls_data) WITH KEY id = 100.
IF sy-subrc = 0.
    DATA(lv_name) = ls_data-name.
ENDIF.

" Modern
DATA(lv_name) = lt_data[ id = 100 ]-name.
" Si no existe, dispara cx_sy_itab_line_not_found
```

Envolver en TRY-CATCH para safe:
```abap
TRY.
    DATA(lv_name) = lt_data[ id = 100 ]-name.
CATCH cx_sy_itab_line_not_found.
    lv_name = 'N/A'.
ENDTRY.
```

### 7. VALUE (constructor)
```abap
DATA(lt_data) = VALUE tt_products(
    ( product_id = '001' name = 'A' price = 100 )
    ( product_id = '002' name = 'B' price = 200 )
    ( product_id = '003' name = 'C' price = 300 )
).
```

Más conciso que APPEND múltiples.

### 8. FOR ... IN (iterator)
```abap
DATA(lt_ids) = VALUE tt_ids(
    FOR ls_prod IN lt_products WHERE ( active = abap_true )
    ( ls_prod-id )
).
```

Equivalente a LOOP + APPEND, más funcional.

### 9. REDUCE (agregación)
```abap
DATA(lv_total) = REDUCE p( INIT sum = 0
                          FOR ls_row IN lt_products
                          NEXT sum = sum + ls_row-price ).
```

Sum, count, max, etc.

## Anti-patterns

### ❌ Nested loops O(n²)
```abap
LOOP AT lt_orders ASSIGNING <o>.
    LOOP AT lt_items ASSIGNING <i> WHERE order_id = <o>-id.
        " O(n * m) → puede ser catastrophic con muchos items
    ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
```

**Mejor**: pre-index lt_items por order_id (sorted/hashed key) → O(n + m).

### ❌ SELECT en loop
```abap
LOOP AT lt_orders ASSIGNING <o>.
    SELECT SINGLE * FROM kna1 INTO @DATA(ls_customer)
        WHERE kunnr = @<o>-customer_id.
    ...
ENDLOOP.
```

N llamadas a DB. Cada una round-trip.

**Mejor**: FOR ALL ENTRIES para traer todos los customers upfront.

### ❌ Ignorar sort
```abap
DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_row.
" ...poblar sin orden...
READ TABLE lt_data WITH KEY id = 100 BINARY SEARCH.
" No garantiza correctness — necesita SORT antes
```

## Common issues

### 'Duplicate key exception'
Insertar dupe en hashed/sorted UNIQUE:
```abap
TRY.
    INSERT VALUE #( id = 100 ) INTO TABLE lt_hashed.
CATCH cx_sy_itab_duplicate_key.
    " Handle dup
ENDTRY.
```

### 'Table expression not found'
```abap
DATA(lv_x) = lt_data[ id = 999 ].
" cx_sy_itab_line_not_found si no existe
```

Envolver en TRY-CATCH o usar READ TABLE tradicional.

### 'Slow con millones de rows'
- Cambiar a HASHED
- Usar secondary keys
- Considerar procesamiento en HANA (AMDP)

## Memory
Itabs live en heap:
- STANDARD: bajo overhead
- SORTED: index adicional
- HASHED: hash table (más memoria)

Para millones de rows en memory: preferir HANA (AMDP/CDS).

## Best practices
- **HASHED para lookups** repetidos por key
- **SORTED para range queries** + acceso ordenado
- **STANDARD default** — cuando no hay razón específica
- **Field symbols** siempre para performance
- **LOOP WHERE** en vez de IF interno
- **FOR ALL ENTRIES** en vez de SELECT en loop
- **SORT antes de BINARY SEARCH**
- **Table expressions** para código legible moderno
- **Secondary keys** para hybrid access patterns

title: ABAP: SmartForms + Adobe Forms — formularios impresos
tags: abap, smartforms, adobe forms, print, form, pdf
excerpt: Diseño de formularios (factura, PO, contract) con SmartForms y Adobe Forms.
body:
## Tecnologías de forms en SAP

### SAPscript (legacy)
Original. Aún en muchos systems. Difícil de mantener.

### SmartForms
Replacement de SAPscript. Editor visual, más productivo.

### Adobe Interactive Forms (AIF) / Adobe Forms
Basado en LiveCycle Designer + PDF. Mejor UX visual.

## SmartForms

### SE71 vs SMARTFORMS
- **SE71** — SAPscript (legacy)
- **SMARTFORMS** — transacción para SmartForms

### Crear form
1. `SMARTFORMS`
2. Form name: `Z_INVOICE_FORM`
3. **Create**

### Estructura
- **Global settings**
  - **Form attributes** — descripción, output options
  - **Form interface** — parameters del form (import/export/tables/exceptions)
  - **Global definitions** — variables + code global
- **Pages + windows** — layout físico

### Form interface
Parameters que recibe el form:
```
Import parameters:
    is_invoice TYPE zinvoice_header

Tables:
    lt_items TYPE zinvoice_items_tt

Exceptions:
    error_processing
```

### Pages
Page 1 = 'FIRST' (default)
- **Windows**: áreas rectangulares con contenido

#### Main window
Window especial — se repite en múltiples pages si el content no cabe. Contiene la tabla de items típicamente.

### Elementos
En windows:
- **Text** — text con placeholders
- **Table** — para items
- **Template** — layout de celdas fijo
- **Loop** — iterar sobre una tabla
- **Command** — condicional / control flow
- **Program lines** — código ABAP embedded
- **Graphic** — imágenes (logos)
- **Address** — formato de dirección

### Text con placeholders
```
Factura: &IS_INVOICE-INVOICE_NUMBER&
Fecha: &IS_INVOICE-INVOICE_DATE&
Cliente: &IS_INVOICE-CUSTOMER_NAME&
```

Opciones de formato: `&IS_INVOICE-AMOUNT(C)&` (currency format).

### Table with loop
```
Loop over: LT_ITEMS
Each item:
    ─────────────────────────────
    | Item &SY-TABIX& | &LT_ITEMS-MATERIAL& | &LT_ITEMS-QTY& | &LT_ITEMS-AMOUNT(C)& |
    ─────────────────────────────
```

### Command (conditional)
```
IF &IS_INVOICE-STATUS& = 'PAID'.
    Text: PAGADO
ELSE.
    Text: PENDIENTE DE PAGO
ENDIF.
```

## Ejecutar SmartForm desde ABAP
```abap
DATA: lv_fm_name TYPE rs38l_fnam.

" Get function module associated with form
CALL FUNCTION 'SSF_FUNCTION_MODULE_NAME'
    EXPORTING formname = 'Z_INVOICE_FORM'
    IMPORTING fm_name = lv_fm_name.

" Call form
CALL FUNCTION lv_fm_name
    EXPORTING is_invoice = ls_invoice
              control_parameters = VALUE ssfctrlop( no_dialog = 'X' preview = 'X' )
              output_options = VALUE ssfcompop( tddest = 'LOCL' )
    TABLES lt_items = lt_items.
```

## Output devices
SAPscript / SmartForms genera **spool request**:
- Print física (SP01)
- Preview
- Save as PDF

### Convert to PDF
```abap
CALL FUNCTION 'CONVERT_OTFSPOOLJOB_2_PDF'
    EXPORTING src_spoolid = lv_spool_id
    TABLES pdf = lt_pdf.

" lt_pdf now contiene PDF binary
" Guardar a archivo:
CALL FUNCTION 'GUI_DOWNLOAD'
    EXPORTING filename = 'C:\invoice.pdf'
              filetype = 'BIN'
    TABLES data_tab = lt_pdf.
```

## Adobe Forms

### Ventajas vs SmartForms
- Diseño visual mejor (LiveCycle Designer)
- PDF nativo
- Interactive forms (user puede llenar en PDF)
- Mejor manejo de layouts complex

### Requisitos
- ADS (Adobe Document Services) instalado en el system
- LiveCycle Designer para diseño

### Crear Adobe Form
1. `SFP` — Form Builder
2. **Interface**: como SmartForms
3. **Form**: se abre LiveCycle Designer (client Windows)
4. Diseñar drag/drop
5. Bind fields al interface

### Ejecutar
Similar a SmartForms:
```abap
DATA(lv_fm_name) = fp_function_module_name( 'Z_INVOICE_PDF' ).

CALL FUNCTION lv_fm_name
    EXPORTING is_invoice = ls_invoice
              /1bcdwb/docparams = VALUE #( langu = 'S' country = 'ES' )
    IMPORTING /1bcdwb/formoutput = DATA(ls_output)
    TABLES lt_items = lt_items.

" ls_output-pdf = PDF binary
```

## Output determination
Determinar automáticamente qué form usar según transaction:

### NACE (message determination)
Asociar output type con event:
- Sales order created → NEU → SmartForm/Adobe Form Z_ORDER_CONFIRM
- Billing document → RD00 → Z_INVOICE_FORM

SAP dispara el form automáticamente.

## Fonts + languages
### Standard fonts
- Helvetica, Courier, Times (universales)
- SAP-Barcode fonts

### Custom fonts
1. Upload a Font Library
2. Assign en form
3. Verify en preview

### Multi-language
SmartForm/Adobe supports múltiples languages:
- **Standard texts** (SO10) con multi-language versions
- Field labels via data element labels

## Debug
### SmartForms preview
Desde SMARTFORMS → **Test** → llena parameters → preview PDF.

### Debug en runtime
1. En el program que llama, breakpoint antes del CALL FUNCTION
2. Step into (F5) el FM del form
3. Debug las program lines embedded

## Migración legacy SAPscript → SmartForms

### Utility
`SF_MIGRATE` — migration tool, no siempre perfecto. Requiere revisión manual.

Para forms complex a menudo es más práctico redesignar.

## Common issues

### 'Form no imprime'
- Output device wrong
- Printer offline
- Ver `SP01` para spool status

### 'PDF corrupto'
- Convert failed
- Verify FM CONVERT_OTFSPOOLJOB_2_PDF exit
- Font missing

### 'Fields en blanco'
- Field name en form no matchea interface
- Verify capitalization (SmartForms es case-sensitive)

### 'Adobe Forms error'
- ADS not configured
- License Adobe issue
- Test con FP_TEST_00

### 'SmartForm slow'
- Muchas iteraciones en loops nested
- Optimize interface data + preprocess data en programa antes de llamar form

## Email PDF
```abap
" Generar PDF
data(ls_output) = ...

" Crear email
DATA(lt_body) = VALUE soli_tab( ( line = 'Adjunta la factura' ) ).

DATA(lt_pack) = VALUE soxpl_tab( ( transf_bin = 'X' doc_size = 5000 doc_type = 'PDF' ) ).

CALL FUNCTION 'SO_NEW_DOCUMENT_ATT_SEND_API1'
    ...
    TABLES contents_hex = ls_output-pdf
           packing_list = lt_pack
           receivers = lt_recv
           contents_txt = lt_body.
```

Adjunta PDF al email.

## Best practices
- **SmartForms** para forms modernos on-prem
- **Adobe Forms** para forms complex o interactive
- **Preview siempre** antes de deploy a PRD
- **Multi-language** desde el inicio si aplica
- **Corporate branding** — logo, colors, fonts consistent
- **Test con data real** — no solo test data
- **Version control** — SmartForms viajan en transportes

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` — dev
- `S_PRINTER` — imprimir
- Auth específica del business flow que llama al form

title: ABAP: batch input y BDC (SM35)
tags: abap, batch input, bdc, sm35, sm31, automation
excerpt: Automatizar transacciones ABAP con Batch Data Communication.
body:
## BDC
Batch Data Communication — automatizar transacciones SAP simulando input de user.

Útil cuando:
- No hay BAPI/RFC disponible para la operación
- Migración masiva de datos legacy
- Interfaces con systems externos que solo saben transacciones

## Herramientas
### SHDB — recording
Graba una transacción con datos manuales, genera code ABAP.

### SM35 — session monitor
Ejecuta sessions BDC, ver logs, reprocesar failures.

### CALL TRANSACTION
Ejecutar transaction desde ABAP con datos.

### Session method
Grabar en table BDCMSGCOLL, ejecutar en batch después.

## Recording con SHDB

### Grabar
1. `SHDB` → **New Recording**
2. Nombre recording: `ZREC_MM01_CREATE_MATERIAL`
3. Transaction: `MM01`
4. Client: 100 (o el que uses)
5. Start recording
6. SAP ejecuta MM01 → tú completás como usuario normal
7. Save → SAP graba cada screen + field + valor
8. Stop recording

### Generate program
SHDB → recording → **Program** button → genera código ABAP con BDCDATA.

### Estructura de BDCDATA
```abap
DATA: lt_bdc TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF bdcdata,
      ls_bdc TYPE bdcdata.

" Screen 100
ls_bdc-program = 'SAPLMGMM'.
ls_bdc-dynpro = '0060'.
ls_bdc-dynbegin = 'X'.
APPEND ls_bdc TO lt_bdc.
CLEAR ls_bdc.

" Field values en Screen 100
ls_bdc-fnam = 'RMMG1-MATNR'.
ls_bdc-fval = '100001'.
APPEND ls_bdc TO lt_bdc.

ls_bdc-fnam = 'RMMG1-MBRSH'.
ls_bdc-fval = 'M'.
APPEND ls_bdc TO lt_bdc.

" User command (usually 'BU' = save = Ctrl+S)
ls_bdc-fnam = 'BDC_OKCODE'.
ls_bdc-fval = '/00'.   " Enter
APPEND ls_bdc TO lt_bdc.

" Screen siguiente...
ls_bdc-program = 'SAPLMGMM'.
ls_bdc-dynpro = '0070'.
ls_bdc-dynbegin = 'X'.
APPEND ls_bdc TO lt_bdc.
CLEAR ls_bdc.

" ... y así sucesivamente
```

## Ejecutar con CALL TRANSACTION (immediate)
```abap
CALL TRANSACTION 'MM01'
    USING lt_bdc
    MODE 'N'    " N=Nothing, A=All screens, E=Error only
    UPDATE 'S'  " S=Synchronous, A=Async
    MESSAGES INTO lt_messages.

IF sy-subrc = 0.
    WRITE: 'Material creado'.
ELSE.
    LOOP AT lt_messages INTO DATA(ls_msg).
        WRITE: / ls_msg-msgtyp, ls_msg-msgid, ls_msg-msgnr, ls_msg-msgv1.
    ENDLOOP.
ENDIF.
```

### Mode
- **A (All screens)**: user ve cada screen (debugging)
- **E (Error only)**: solo si hay error, muestra screen problematic
- **N (Nothing)**: silent, no user interaction — production

## Session method (BDC_OPEN_GROUP)
Más robusto para volume grande — permite reprocessing:

```abap
CALL FUNCTION 'BDC_OPEN_GROUP'
    EXPORTING client = sy-mandt
              group = 'ZMASS_MAT_CREATE'
              user = sy-uname.

" Para cada material a crear:
LOOP AT lt_materials INTO ls_material.
    fill_bdcdata( CHANGING ct_bdc = lt_bdc ).

    CALL FUNCTION 'BDC_INSERT'
        EXPORTING tcode = 'MM01'
        TABLES dynprotab = lt_bdc.
ENDLOOP.

CALL FUNCTION 'BDC_CLOSE_GROUP'.
```

### Ejecutar la session
`SM35` → seleccionar `ZMASS_MAT_CREATE` → **Process**:
- **Foreground** (F5) — user ve todo, útil para debug
- **Display errors only** (F6) — solo interviene si error
- **Background** (F8) — silent, para production

### Reprocesar failures
Si hay errors:
- SM35 → session → **Process** → botón **Process/foreground** en error records
- User arregla manual, session continúa

## CALL TRANSACTION vs Session

### CALL TRANSACTION
- Immediate
- No queda en SM35
- No re-processable
- Rápido

### Session (BDC_OPEN_GROUP)
- Queue en SM35
- Re-processable
- Ver logs históricos
- Preferido para masivo o auditable

## LSMW (Legacy System Migration Workbench)
Herramienta más completa para migration:
- Batch input recordings
- Field mapping
- Data conversion
- Business Objects (BAPIs)

`LSMW` — deprecated en S/4HANA (reemplazado por Migration Cockpit LTMC).

## Detección de errors

### Ver session log
SM35 → session → **Log** button:
- Records processed OK
- Records failed con error message
- Timestamp

### En CALL TRANSACTION
```abap
CALL TRANSACTION ... MESSAGES INTO lt_messages.

READ TABLE lt_messages WITH KEY msgtyp = 'E' INTO DATA(ls_err).
IF sy-subrc = 0.
    " Error found
ENDIF.
```

## Best practices

### 1. Preferir BAPI sobre BDC
BAPI (Business API) es preferred:
- Más rápido
- Sin dependency en pantalla
- Robust ante cambios SAP

Ejemplo: `BAPI_MATERIAL_SAVEDATA` en vez de BDC de MM01.

### 2. Cuando NO hay BAPI
- Recording BDC
- Documentar bien el flujo
- Considerar impacto de future upgrades SAP (screens pueden cambiar)

### 3. Test con volumen realistic
Antes de PRD, test con miles de records.

### 4. Idempotency
Si BDC re-ejecuta, no debe duplicar. Add checks 'exists' antes de create.

### 5. Error handling
No abortar en primer error. Log + continue.

### 6. Performance
- Session method para volumen grande
- CALL TRANSACTION MODE N para speed
- UPDATE 'S' vs 'A': sync más seguro pero más lento

## Common issues

### 'Screen no aparece igual'
- SAP updated the screen
- BDC recording desactualizado → regrabar
- Nuevos required fields

### 'Message: Field not found'
- Wrong field name en BDC
- Field visible solo con specific setup

### 'Data type mismatch'
- BDC pasa todo como string
- Verify conversion (dates, amounts)

### 'Slow BDC'
- MODE 'A' o 'E' interrumpe con screen — usar 'N' para production
- UPDATE 'A' (async) puede ser más rápido pero menos confiable

## Autorización
- `S_TCODE` — para la transacción que se ejecuta
- `S_BDC_MONI` — SM35 access
- User técnico dedicado suele hacer los BDC masivos

## Alternativa moderna
Para S/4HANA: Migration Cockpit (LTMC) reemplaza LSMW.

BDC sigue funcional pero para new integrations → OData / RFC / BAPI preferido.

title: ABAP: message classes (SE91) — sistema centralizado de mensajes
tags: abap, message, se91, message class, i18n
body:
## Message class
Contenedor de mensajes usados en todo el programa (o multiple programas).

### Beneficios
- Traducciones automáticas
- Cambios centrales (edit uno vez, applies everywhere)
- Consistencia
- Search-by-code cuando debug

## Crear message class

### SE91
1. `SE91` → **Message class**: `ZMYMSG`
2. **Create**
3. Attributes: descripción
4. Tab **Messages**:
   - **Message no**: 001
   - **Message short text**: `Precio no puede ser negativo`
   - Optional: **Self-explanatory** checkbox

### Placeholders
Mensajes pueden tener &1, &2, &3, &4:
```
Message 010: 'El material &1 no existe en plant &2'
```

## Uso en ABAP

### MESSAGE statement
```abap
MESSAGE e001(zmymsg).
" 'Precio no puede ser negativo' → error
```

### Con placeholders
```abap
MESSAGE e010(zmymsg) WITH iv_material iv_plant.
" 'El material 100001 no existe en plant WERK'
```

### Message types
- **A** — Abort — mata programa immediately
- **E** — Error — stop flow
- **W** — Warning — user puede continue
- **I** — Information — dialog OK
- **S** — Success — footer message
- **X** — Exit — dump (nunca usar en business)

## Message en RAP / OData
```abap
METHOD validate.
    APPEND VALUE #( %tky = key-%tky
                    %msg = new_message(
                        id = 'ZMYMSG'
                        number = '010'
                        severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                        v1 = ls_material-name
                        v2 = ls_material-plant )
                  ) TO reported-material.
ENDMETHOD.
```

El user en Fiori ve el message.

## Message en class de exception
```abap
CLASS z_cx_business DEFINITION
    PUBLIC
    INHERITING FROM cx_static_check
    CREATE PUBLIC.

    PUBLIC SECTION.
        INTERFACES if_t100_message.

        CONSTANTS: BEGIN OF material_not_found,
                       msgid TYPE symsgid  VALUE 'ZMYMSG',
                       msgno TYPE symsgno  VALUE '010',
                       attr1 TYPE scx_attrname VALUE 'MATERIAL',
                       attr2 TYPE scx_attrname VALUE 'PLANT',
                   END OF material_not_found.

        DATA material TYPE string.
        DATA plant TYPE string.

        METHODS constructor
            IMPORTING textid LIKE if_t100_message=>t100key OPTIONAL
                     material TYPE string OPTIONAL
                     plant TYPE string OPTIONAL.
ENDCLASS.
```

Uso:
```abap
RAISE EXCEPTION NEW z_cx_business(
    textid = z_cx_business=>material_not_found
    material = '100001'
    plant = 'WERK1'
).
```

Exception `get_text( )` devuelve message con placeholders resueltos.

## Multi-language

### Traducir
`SE91` → mensaje → menú **Translate**.

### Auto en runtime
SAP muestra el message en el logon language del user.

### Fallback
Si language no está traducido → default (usually English).

## Long text
Mensajes pueden tener **long text** — explicación detallada + hint de solución:

1. SE91 → mensaje → **Long text** button
2. Escribir explicación
3. Save

User en el dialog puede ver el long text con F1.

## Search messages
En SE91:
- Number: 001
- Text: 'precio'

Buscar por content en toda la message class.

## Naming convention
### Message class
- `Z<Modulo>_<Purpose>_MSG` — ej: `ZMM_MASTER_MSG`, `ZFI_POSTING_MSG`

### Message number
- **001-099**: general errors
- **100-199**: validation warnings
- **200-299**: info messages
- **300-399**: success messages

Convención opcional pero útil.

## Ejemplos comunes

### Validaciones
```
010: 'Field & es obligatorio'
011: 'Valor & fuera de rango permitido (& a &)'
012: 'Ya existe un registro con clave &'
```

### Estados
```
020: 'Documento & bloqueado por usuario &'
021: 'Solicitud & aprobada por &'
022: 'Documento & anulado el & por &'
```

### Info
```
100: 'Se procesaron & registros correctamente'
101: 'Se creó el documento &'
```

### Success
```
200: 'Guardado correctamente'
201: '& registros creados'
```

## Common issues

### 'Message no muestra placeholder'
- Placeholder mal ubicado (&1 vs &)
- No pasás WITH values
- Type mismatch

### 'Message aparece en English'
- Not translated to language del user
- Traducir en SE91 → Translate

### 'Long text no aparece'
- No configurado
- User no clic en F1

## Migration de hardcoded strings

### Antipattern
```abap
IF lv_price < 0.
    MESSAGE 'El precio no puede ser negativo' TYPE 'E'.
ENDIF.
```

### Fix
```abap
IF lv_price < 0.
    MESSAGE e001(zmymsg).
ENDIF.
```

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` con object type `MSAG` — crear/modificar message classes
- Runtime: cualquier user puede recibir messages

## Best practices
- **Todos los messages en class** — nunca hardcoded strings
- **Placeholders** — más claros con context
- **Long text** para errors comunes — help al user
- **Traducciones** — al menos en idiomas de tu org
- **Naming convention** consistent
- **Reuse** — antes de crear nuevo, buscar si existe
- **Cleanup** — remover messages obsoletos

## Transport
Message classes viajan como cualquier objeto ABAP (transport request DEVK...).

## Docs
SAP Help: **ABAP Messages**

title: ABAP: field symbols + data references
tags: abap, field symbol, data reference, generic, dynamic
excerpt: Field symbols + refs — power features de ABAP.
body:
## Field symbols
Pointer a memory. No copy, referencia directa.

### Declarar
```abap
FIELD-SYMBOLS: <fs_string> TYPE string,
               <fs_row>    TYPE ty_product,
               <fs_any>    TYPE any.        " genérico
```

### Assign
```abap
DATA lv_x TYPE string VALUE 'hello'.
ASSIGN lv_x TO <fs_string>.
<fs_string> = 'world'.   " cambia lv_x
```

### LOOP AT ... ASSIGNING
Más eficiente que INTO (no copia):
```abap
LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<row>).
    <row>-processed = 'X'.   " modifica lt_data directamente
ENDLOOP.
```

Sin field symbol:
```abap
LOOP AT lt_data INTO DATA(ls_row).
    ls_row-processed = 'X'.
    MODIFY lt_data FROM ls_row.
ENDLOOP.
```

Field symbol es 2-3x más rápido.

### Type any (genérico)
```abap
FIELD-SYMBOLS <fs> TYPE any.
ASSIGN lv_x TO <fs>.
" <fs> now points to lv_x, type resuelto en runtime
```

Útil en dynamic programming.

### Assign component
Acceso a field dinámicamente por nombre:
```abap
DATA: BEGIN OF ls_data,
          matnr TYPE mara-matnr,
          werks TYPE marc-werks,
      END OF ls_data.

FIELD-SYMBOLS <fs> TYPE any.

ASSIGN COMPONENT 'MATNR' OF STRUCTURE ls_data TO <fs>.
<fs> = '100001'.

ASSIGN COMPONENT 'WERKS' OF STRUCTURE ls_data TO <fs>.
<fs> = 'PLANT1'.
```

Component name puede venir de variable → **dynamic field access**.

### ASSIGN CASTING
Interpretar memory con distinto type:
```abap
DATA lv_string TYPE string VALUE '20260728'.
FIELD-SYMBOLS <fs_date> TYPE d.
ASSIGN lv_string TO <fs_date> CASTING.
" <fs_date> = 20260728 (as date)
```

## Data references (data refs)
Apuntadores tipados como en C++.

### Declarar
```abap
DATA lr_product TYPE REF TO ty_product.
DATA lr_any TYPE REF TO data.        " genérico
```

### Crear
```abap
CREATE DATA lr_product.
lr_product->matnr = '100001'.
" O:
CREATE DATA lr_any TYPE ty_product.
```

### Access via dereference
```abap
lr_product->matnr = '100001'.

" O:
FIELD-SYMBOLS <fs> TYPE ty_product.
ASSIGN lr_product->* TO <fs>.
```

### Get reference
```abap
GET REFERENCE OF ls_data INTO lr_product.
" lr_product ahora apunta a ls_data
```

### CAST
```abap
DATA lr_generic TYPE REF TO data.
CREATE DATA lr_generic TYPE ty_product.

DATA lr_specific TYPE REF TO ty_product.
lr_specific ?= lr_generic.   " downcast
```

## Dynamic tables
### Crear itab dinámicamente
```abap
DATA lr_table TYPE REF TO data.
FIELD-SYMBOLS <lt_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

DATA(lo_structdescr) = cl_abap_structdescr=>create( 
    components = VALUE #(
        ( name = 'MATNR' type = cl_abap_elemdescr=>get_c( 18 ) )
        ( name = 'NAME' type = cl_abap_elemdescr=>get_string( ) )
    )
).

DATA(lo_tabledescr) = cl_abap_tabledescr=>create( p_line_type = lo_structdescr ).

CREATE DATA lr_table TYPE HANDLE lo_tabledescr.
ASSIGN lr_table->* TO <lt_table>.
```

Ahora `<lt_table>` es una itab dinámica.

## Uso avanzado

### RTTI / RTTS (Runtime Type Info / Services)
`CL_ABAP_TYPEDESCR` y subclasses para introspection.

### Introspection
```abap
DATA(lo_typedescr) = cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_data( ls_data ).

CASE lo_typedescr->type_kind.
    WHEN cl_abap_typedescr=>typekind_int.
        " es integer
    WHEN cl_abap_typedescr=>typekind_string.
        " es string
    WHEN cl_abap_typedescr=>typekind_struct1 OR cl_abap_typedescr=>typekind_struct2.
        " es structure
ENDCASE.
```

### Get all fields of a structure
```abap
DATA(lo_structdescr) = CAST cl_abap_structdescr( 
    cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_data( ls_data ) ).

LOOP AT lo_structdescr->components INTO DATA(ls_component).
    WRITE: / ls_component-name, ls_component-type_kind.
ENDLOOP.
```

Útil para generic reports, exports, etc.

## Patterns comunes

### Modify record en itab sin work area
```abap
LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<row>) WHERE status = 'PENDING'.
    <row>-status = 'PROCESSED'.
    <row>-processed_at = sy-datum.
ENDLOOP.
```

### Dynamic where clause
```abap
DATA lv_where TYPE string.
lv_where = |matnr = '{ iv_matnr }' AND werks = '{ iv_werks }'|.

DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF marc.
SELECT * FROM marc WHERE (lv_where) INTO TABLE @lt_data.
```

### Generic method
```abap
METHOD process_data.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_data> TYPE STANDARD TABLE,
                   <ls_row>  TYPE any.

    ASSIGN it_data TO <lt_data>.

    LOOP AT <lt_data> ASSIGNING <ls_row>.
        ASSIGN COMPONENT 'STATUS' OF STRUCTURE <ls_row> TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<status>).
        IF sy-subrc = 0.
            <status> = 'PROCESSED'.
        ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
ENDMETHOD.
```

Recibe cualquier itab con field `STATUS` y lo actualiza.

## Common pitfalls

### 'FIELD-SYMBOL is not assigned'
Access sin assign previo → dump `GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED`.

```abap
IF <fs> IS ASSIGNED.
    " safe access
ENDIF.
```

### 'Type conflict'
CASTING con types incompatibles → dump.

Verify types con RTTI antes.

### 'MODIFY not respected'
Field symbol modifies directly, no need MODIFY.

### 'Reference not resolved'
Data ref sin CREATE DATA → dump.

## Performance
- **Field symbol > work area** para bulk operations
- **Data ref** util para trees, linked lists
- **RTTI** tiene overhead — no en tight loops

## Common issues

### 'Cannot ASSIGN COMPONENT'
- Component doesn't exist en structure
- SY-SUBRC check important

### 'Data reference no longer valid'
- Referenced data was garbage collected
- Or scope terminated

## Best practices
- **Field symbols para performance** en loops
- **Data refs para OO patterns** (linked structures)
- **RTTI para generic code**
- **Check ASSIGNED / IS BOUND** antes de acceso
- **Type any solo cuando genérico requerido**
- **CASTING con cuidado** — type safety importante

## Autorización
No específica — features del lenguaje ABAP.

title: ABAP OO: clases, interfaces, herencia
body:
## Class
Unidad OO. Encapsula data + behavior.

### Estructura
```abap
CLASS zcl_order DEFINITION
    PUBLIC
    FINAL
    CREATE PUBLIC.

    PUBLIC SECTION.
        TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_item,
                   material TYPE matnr,
                   qty      TYPE i,
               END OF ty_item.

        DATA: order_id  TYPE i READ-ONLY,
              customer  TYPE kna1-kunnr,
              items     TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item.

        METHODS:
            constructor IMPORTING iv_customer TYPE kna1-kunnr,
            add_item    IMPORTING is_item TYPE ty_item,
            get_total   RETURNING VALUE(rv_total) TYPE p LENGTH 10 DECIMALS 2.

    PROTECTED SECTION.
        DATA: order_status TYPE c LENGTH 1.

    PRIVATE SECTION.
        METHODS: validate_customer IMPORTING iv_customer TYPE kna1-kunnr
                                   RAISING zcx_invalid_customer.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_order IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD constructor.
        validate_customer( iv_customer ).
        customer = iv_customer.
        order_id = generate_id( ).
        order_status = 'D'.   " draft
    ENDMETHOD.

    METHOD add_item.
        APPEND is_item TO items.
    ENDMETHOD.

    METHOD get_total.
        LOOP AT items INTO DATA(ls_item).
            rv_total = rv_total + ( ls_item-qty * get_price( ls_item-material ) ).
        ENDLOOP.
    ENDMETHOD.

    METHOD validate_customer.
        SELECT SINGLE @abap_true FROM kna1 INTO @DATA(lv_exists)
            WHERE kunnr = @iv_customer.
        IF lv_exists = abap_false.
            RAISE EXCEPTION NEW zcx_invalid_customer( iv_customer = iv_customer ).
        ENDIF.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
```

### Visibilidad
- **PUBLIC** — accessible desde any code
- **PROTECTED** — subclasses only
- **PRIVATE** — la clase misma only

### Usar la clase
```abap
TRY.
    DATA(lo_order) = NEW zcl_order( iv_customer = '1000' ).
    lo_order->add_item( VALUE #( material = '100001' qty = 5 ) ).
    DATA(lv_total) = lo_order->get_total( ).
    WRITE: 'Total:', lv_total.

CATCH zcx_invalid_customer INTO DATA(lx).
    WRITE: 'Error:', lx->get_text( ).
ENDTRY.
```

## Static
### Static members (no requieren instance)
```abap
CLASS zcl_util DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        CLASS-METHODS format_currency 
            IMPORTING iv_amount TYPE p
            RETURNING VALUE(rv_formatted) TYPE string.

        CLASS-DATA config TYPE zconfig.
ENDCLASS.

" Uso:
DATA(lv_str) = zcl_util=>format_currency( 1500 ).
```

## Interface
Contract que las clases implementan.

```abap
INTERFACE zif_shape.
    METHODS: get_area RETURNING VALUE(rv_area) TYPE p LENGTH 10 DECIMALS 2,
             get_perimeter RETURNING VALUE(rv_perimeter) TYPE p LENGTH 10 DECIMALS 2.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_circle DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        INTERFACES zif_shape.
        METHODS constructor IMPORTING iv_radius TYPE p.
    PRIVATE SECTION.
        DATA radius TYPE p LENGTH 10 DECIMALS 2.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_circle IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD constructor. radius = iv_radius. ENDMETHOD.

    METHOD zif_shape~get_area.
        rv_area = '3.14159' * radius * radius.
    ENDMETHOD.

    METHOD zif_shape~get_perimeter.
        rv_perimeter = 2 * '3.14159' * radius.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
```

### Polymorphism
```abap
DATA lt_shapes TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF REF TO zif_shape.

APPEND NEW zcl_circle( 5 ) TO lt_shapes.
APPEND NEW zcl_rectangle( 10, 20 ) TO lt_shapes.
APPEND NEW zcl_triangle( 3, 4, 5 ) TO lt_shapes.

LOOP AT lt_shapes INTO DATA(lo_shape).
    WRITE: / lo_shape->get_area( ), lo_shape->get_perimeter( ).
ENDLOOP.
```

Cada shape ejecuta su implementation.

## Inheritance
```abap
CLASS zcl_animal DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS: constructor IMPORTING iv_name TYPE string,
                 speak      " abstract concept — subclass implements
                     REDEFINITION_ALLOWED.
    PROTECTED SECTION.
        DATA name TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_animal IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD constructor. name = iv_name. ENDMETHOD.
    METHOD speak.
        WRITE: 'Generic animal sound'.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dog DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_animal.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS: speak REDEFINITION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dog IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD speak.
        WRITE: / |{ name }: Woof!|.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_cat DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_animal.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS: speak REDEFINITION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_cat IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD speak.
        WRITE: / |{ name }: Meow|.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
```

### Uso
```abap
DATA(lt_animals) = VALUE tt_animals(
    ( NEW zcl_dog( 'Rex' ) )
    ( NEW zcl_cat( 'Whiskers' ) )
).

LOOP AT lt_animals INTO DATA(lo_animal).
    lo_animal->speak( ).
ENDLOOP.
```

### Super
```abap
METHOD speak.
    super->speak( ).   " call parent implementation
    WRITE: / 'and also...'.
ENDMETHOD.
```

## Abstract class
```abap
CLASS zcl_animal DEFINITION ABSTRACT.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS speak ABSTRACT.
ENDCLASS.
```

No se puede instantiate. Solo subclasses concretas.

## Friend classes
Otro class con access a private members:
```abap
CLASS zcl_bank DEFINITION FRIENDS zcl_auditor.
    PRIVATE SECTION.
        DATA balance TYPE p.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_auditor DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS audit IMPORTING io_bank TYPE REF TO zcl_bank.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_auditor IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD audit.
        WRITE: 'Balance:', io_bank->balance.   " access private
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
```

## Events
```abap
CLASS zcl_button DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        EVENTS clicked EXPORTING VALUE(iv_id) TYPE i.
        METHODS on_click.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_button IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD on_click.
        RAISE EVENT clicked EXPORTING iv_id = 100.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

" Handler class
CLASS zcl_handler DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS handle_click FOR EVENT clicked OF zcl_button
            IMPORTING iv_id.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_handler IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD handle_click.
        WRITE: 'Button clicked:', iv_id.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

" Uso
DATA(lo_btn) = NEW zcl_button( ).
DATA(lo_handler) = NEW zcl_handler( ).
SET HANDLER lo_handler->handle_click FOR lo_btn.
lo_btn->on_click( ).
```

## Singleton
```abap
CLASS zcl_config DEFINITION
    CREATE PRIVATE.   " no external CREATE

    PUBLIC SECTION.
        CLASS-METHODS get_instance
            RETURNING VALUE(ro_instance) TYPE REF TO zcl_config.

        METHODS get_value IMPORTING iv_key TYPE string
                          RETURNING VALUE(rv_value) TYPE string.

    PRIVATE SECTION.
        CLASS-DATA instance TYPE REF TO zcl_config.
        DATA config_map TYPE hashed_config_tt WITH UNIQUE KEY key.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_config IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD get_instance.
        IF instance IS NOT BOUND.
            instance = NEW #( ).
            instance->load_from_db( ).
        ENDIF.
        ro_instance = instance.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
```

## Factory
```abap
CLASS zcl_shape_factory DEFINITION.
    PUBLIC SECTION.
        CLASS-METHODS create
            IMPORTING iv_type TYPE string
            RETURNING VALUE(ro_shape) TYPE REF TO zif_shape
            RAISING zcx_unknown_shape.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_shape_factory IMPLEMENTATION.
    METHOD create.
        CASE iv_type.
            WHEN 'CIRCLE'.
                ro_shape = NEW zcl_circle( 5 ).
            WHEN 'RECT'.
                ro_shape = NEW zcl_rectangle( 10, 20 ).
            WHEN OTHERS.
                RAISE EXCEPTION NEW zcx_unknown_shape( iv_type = iv_type ).
        ENDCASE.
    ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
```

## Best practices
- **PRIVATE por default** — expose solo lo necesario
- **Constructor validates** — object siempre en state consistente
- **Interfaces over inheritance** — composition preferred
- **Small classes** — single responsibility
- **Immutable when possible** — READ-ONLY attributes
- **Test with ABAP Unit** — cada method
- **Naming**: `ZCL_<Modulo>_<Purpose>` para classes, `ZIF_...` para interfaces

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` con object type CLAS o INTF

title: ABAP: SmartForms, SapScript, Adobe — decidir cuál usar
tags: abap, forms, decision, sapscript, smartforms, adobe
excerpt: Comparación de tecnologías de formularios en SAP.
body:
## Contexto
En SAP hay 3 tecnologías activas para forms impresos + PDFs:

### 1. SAPscript (SE71)
- Original (~1990)
- Text-based, syntax-heavy
- Legacy pero widespread

### 2. SmartForms (SMARTFORMS)
- Reemplaza SAPscript (~2000)
- Editor visual mejorado
- Standard en muchas orgs

### 3. Adobe Interactive Forms (SFP)
- Basado en LiveCycle Designer + PDF
- Best UX visual
- Interactive PDF forms posibles

## Comparación

| Feature | SAPscript | SmartForms | Adobe Forms |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Editor visual | ❌ (text) | ✅ (SE) | ✅ (LiveCycle Designer) |
| Learning curve | Alta | Media | Baja-Media |
| Multi-language | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Barcodes | Limited | ✅ | ✅ |
| Interactive PDF | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (fillable) |
| Fonts custom | Limited | ✅ | ✅ |
| Requires ADS | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (Adobe Document Services) |
| Costo license | Included | Included | ADS license required |
| Modification-friendly | Moderate | Moderate | High |
| Recommended new dev | ❌ | Yes | Yes (para complex) |

## Cuándo usar SAPscript
### Sí
- Sistema legacy con muchos SAPscript existentes
- Cambios menores a forms existentes

### No
- Nuevos desarrollos → prefer SmartForms/Adobe

## Cuándo usar SmartForms
### Sí
- Facturas, purchase orders, delivery notes
- Layouts moderately complex
- Sin necesidad de PDF interactive
- Team no tiene expertise en Adobe LiveCycle

### No
- Requiere PDF fillable
- Layouts muy complex con images + tablas anidadas
- Sin ADS y precisas Adobe features

## Cuándo usar Adobe Forms
### Sí
- PDF interactive (user llena y submit)
- Layouts complex (multi-column, complex charts)
- Corporate branding strict
- ADS ya instalado

### No
- ADS no disponible
- Formularios muy simples
- Team sin experience en Adobe

## Consideraciones de mantenimiento

### SmartForms
- Editor SAP → cualquier ABAP dev puede modificar
- Sin external tools
- Buen fit para in-house dev team

### Adobe Forms
- Requires LiveCycle Designer instalado
- Curva de aprendizaje adicional
- Con team especialista funciona bien

## Performance

### SAPscript
Rapido en runtime — text-based rendering.

### SmartForms
Similar. Overhead menor por FM wrapper.

### Adobe Forms
Slower por ADS involvement:
- SAP → ADS (HTTP call)
- ADS renders PDF
- Return al SAP

Overhead notable en batches grandes.

## Testing

### Preview de SmartForm
SMARTFORMS → Test button → completa parameters → PDF preview.

### Preview de Adobe Form
SFP → Test → similar.

## Migración legacy → moderno

### SAPscript → SmartForms
- Utility: `SF_MIGRATE`
- No siempre perfect
- Formularios complex may require redesign

### SmartForms → Adobe
- No migration tool automated
- Redesign manual con LiveCycle Designer

## Nueva alternativa: SAP CDS-based forms
SAP moviéndose a:
- **Adobe Forms** (mantiene) para PDF
- **Fiori apps** para digital-first (no impresión)
- **CDS + Analytics** para reports (no forms)

Forms impresos declinan (menos papel) pero seguirán relevant.

## Recomendación por scenario

### Migration a S/4HANA
- Mantener SmartForms/SAPscript existentes que funcionan
- Nuevos forms → Adobe Forms si ADS activo
- Redesignar si aportan valor UI/UX

### Nueva implementación
- **Adobe Forms** si ADS disponible + team con skills
- **SmartForms** si simpler o sin ADS

### Facturación electrónica
- Requerimientos gov-specific pueden dictate technology
- Concur/Facelia/etc. plugins pueden generar XML/PDF fuera de SAP forms

## Fonts corporativos
### SmartForms
Upload font a SAP Font Library. Assign en form.

### Adobe
Instalar fonts en LiveCycle. Embed en PDF.

Corporate fonts (custom typography) mejor soporte en Adobe.

## Barcodes
Muchos usos: labels, invoices con QR:

### SmartForms
SAP-Barcode fonts o Adobe barcode fonts.

### Adobe
Barcode wizard integrado (drag/drop QR, EAN, Code 128).

## Email delivery
Ambos generan PDF que puede attachar a email:

```abap
" Get PDF from SmartForm o Adobe Form
data(lv_pdf_binary) = ...

" Attach + send
CALL FUNCTION 'SO_NEW_DOCUMENT_ATT_SEND_API1' ...
```

## Common issues

### 'Adobe Forms error'
- ADS not configured (`SFP` → **Test**)
- License Adobe issue
- Fonts missing en server

### 'SmartForm slow'
- Complex loops en items
- Optimize interface data before call

### 'PDF corrupto'
- Convert FM issue (SmartForm)
- ADS response error (Adobe)

## Best practices
- **Preview siempre** antes de PRD
- **Multi-language** desde el inicio si aplica
- **Corporate branding** documented
- **Version en Git via abapGit**
- **Test con data real** — no solo test data
- **Naming**: `Z_<Modulo>_<Purpose>_FORM`

## Autorización
- `S_DEVELOP` — dev
- `S_PRINTER` — imprimir
- ADS-specific auth para Adobe Forms

## Docs
- SAP Help: **SmartForms**, **Adobe Interactive Forms**
- OpenSAP course: 'Adobe Forms by Adobe LiveCycle Designer'
